# Regular expression built from HTTP request data (Python)

`qualor:python/regex-injection` · Issue · Severity: Medium · [CWE-1333](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1333.html), [CWE-400](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/400.html)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
HTTP request data used as a regular expression pattern: the pattern argument of `re.compile()`,
`re.search()`, `re.match()`, `re.fullmatch()`, `re.sub()`, `re.subn()`, `re.split()`,
`re.findall()` and `re.finditer()`, in Flask, Django and FastAPI applications. Request data used as
the text to search is fine and not reported.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
Python's regular expression engine backtracks. A crafted pattern such as `(a+)+$` can take
exponential time on a short input and keep a worker busy for minutes, so a handful of requests can
make the service unavailable (ReDoS). A pattern from the client can also simply match more than
intended, for example `.*` in a search that should match one name.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** the search term is used as a pattern.

```python
import re

from flask import Flask, jsonify, request

app = Flask(__name__)

NAMES = ["alice", "bob", "carol"]


@app.route("/search")
def search():
    pattern = request.args["q"]
    return jsonify(names=[n for n in NAMES if re.search(pattern, n)])
```

**Compliant:** the term is escaped, so it matches only itself.

```python
import re

from flask import Flask, jsonify, request

app = Flask(__name__)

NAMES = ["alice", "bob", "carol"]


@app.route("/search")
def search():
    pattern = re.escape(request.args["q"])
    return jsonify(names=[n for n in NAMES if re.search(pattern, n)])
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Escape request text with `re.escape()` before building a pattern from it.
- If users choose between a few patterns, pick the pattern from a fixed allow-list.
- For plain substring search, skip regular expressions: `term in text`.
- Match request data against a constant pattern instead: `re.fullmatch(r"[a-z]+", value)`.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- Flask
- Django
- FastAPI

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- Taint is not carried through a slice (`request.args["q"][:20]`).
- A pattern first validated by a constant regex (`if not re.fullmatch(r"[\w ]+", x): return`) is
  still reported.
- An allow-list is recognised only as a lookup in a module-level dict of literals assigned to an
  upper-case name that is never changed, or as a ternary of constants; a membership check is not.
- Request sources are recognised by their shape: a Flask `<int:n>` route parameter and a numeric
  Django URL argument still count as request data, and a function whose first parameter is named
  `request` in a Django module is taken for a view.
<!-- end: known-limits -->
